name: Nigerian by Birth who Renounced Citizenship Visa (N2A/N2B)

requirements.blocker_text: Proof of former Nigerian citizenship by birth (birth certificate, parentage documentation).
Documents evidencing the formal renunciation of Nigerian citizenship.

outcome.duration_length: indefinite, valid through the holder's passport validity (N2A); N2B (spouse of an N2A holder) shares the same structure

sources.title: Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) -- Permanent Residence Visa categories N2A (Nigerian by Birth who Renounced Nigerian Citizenship) and N2B (their spouse): requires proof of former Nigerian status via birth certificate, renunciation documents, and a valid foreign passport; grants an infinite residence permit valid through passport validity; no employment unless separately authorized

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Nigeria). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- tier-1 NIS sourced, though thin (no fee figures, no exact processing time). This is a RESIDENCE route, not a citizenship-restoration route: it lets a person who was Nigerian by birth and formally renounced that citizenship live in Nigeria again indefinitely, but does NOT itself restore citizenship. NO SEPARATE STATUTORY CITIZENSHIP-RESTORATION/REACQUISITION PROVISION WAS FOUND for former Nigerian citizens in this build -- Nigeria's Constitution (Chapter III) and the Citizenship and Business Department's own materials describe only birth, registration, and naturalisation as acquisition routes, with no distinct 'restoration' pathway for people who previously renounced. A renounced-Nigerian-by-birth wanting citizenship back would, on the evidence found here, need to reapply via ordinary registration or naturalisation like any other applicant -- this is a genuine, disclosed gap rather than an invented mechanism, and the single most likely area where a dedicated administrative procedure exists but wasn't locatable at tier-1/2 in this build. Not to be confused with ng_citizenship_by_descent.json (Section 26(2B), for people who were NEVER themselves Nigerian citizens but have a Nigerian parent/grandparent/great-grandparent).
